problem:
The number of sales $S(t)$ of a new tech device $t$ weeks after the start of sales can be modeled by the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=-0.1S.
$$

If there were $100\,000$ sales initially, calculate the number of sales after $10$ weeks. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

examples.problem:
Suppose that the value $V(t)$ of a particular car can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d V}{\textrm d t} = -0.1V,
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years, since the car was first purchased. If the car was purchased for $\[math]10\,000,$ what will it be worth after $3$ years?
examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that the right-hand side of the equation is *negative*, which means that the car's value is *decreasing.*

This is an exponential decay differential equation with $r = 0.1.$ Therefore, the general solution to this equation is

$$
V(t) = V_0 e^{-0.1 t}.
$$

We know that the car was first purchased for $\[math]10\,000.$ Therefore, $V_0 = 10\,000,$ and we have the particular solution

$$
V(t) = 10\,000 e^{-0.1 t}.
$$

To find the car's value after $3$ years, we substitute $t=3$ into the particular solution above. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}V(3) & =10\,000{e}^{-0.1\cdot 3} \\  & =10\,000{e}^{-0.3} \\  & ≈7\,408.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the car will be worth approximately $\[/math]7\,408$ after three years.

feedback.problem:
The number of insects in a controlled habitat $H(t)$ after $t$ months can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}H}{\text{d}t}=2H.
$$

If there are currently $120$ insects in the habitat, calculate the number of insects after $2$ months. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

The number of insects after $2$ months is approximately 
{{field-1}}
insects.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the number of insects using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}H}{\text{d}t}=2H.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
H(t)={H}_{0}\,{e}^{2t},
$$

where ${H}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that there are currently $120$ insects in the habitat, so we have ${H}_{0}=120.$

Therefore, the number of insects $H$ at time $t$ is

$$
H(t)=120\,{e}^{2t}.
$$

Finally, to find the number of insects when $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}H(2) & =120\,{e}^{2\cdot 2} \\  & =120\,{e}^{4} \\  & ≈6551.78\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that the number of insects after $2$ months is approximately $6552$ insects.
